run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T04:25:04Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects a short burst of failed requests through the proxy. Frontend-proxy's own error-span counters jumped at the 04:19:30Z sample (ingress 519 to 526, router frontend egress 447 to 453), and its access log shows six HTTP 500 responses within 600 ms at 04:17:43Z plus 503 "UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" responses at 04:17:39Z and 04:18:33Z. The six 500s match six ERROR client spans for grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct on the frontend (five product-page requests plus one POST /api/checkout). The burst coincides exactly with the product-catalog Deployment rollout at 04:17:39-43Z, in which ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 replaced product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc and the old pod was stopped at 04:17:43Z; the two ReplicaSets' pod templates are identical apart from the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:17:39Z (a rollout restart, same image digest, same env, same ConfigMap volume). The alert's reported 0.0111 matches roughly 7 failed of about 630 requests (7/630 = 0.01111) in its evaluation window, and a 5-minute 'for' would explain firing at 04:25:04Z, but the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus so that derivation is unverified. product-catalog itself stayed Ready with 0 restarts and recorded no ERROR span status. The flagd fault-injection flag productCatalogFailure is 'on', but the multi-product, single-window error pattern does not match a 'fail on a specific product' fault, so it is reported as an unsupported candidate rather than the cause. A continuing low-rate 503 UC pattern on product and recommendation routes before and after the rollout remains unexplained.

claims.text: frontend-proxy (otel-demo) recorded its own ERROR spans on span_name "ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and "router frontend egress" (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT); the raw ingress error counter rose from 519 to 526 and the egress error counter from 447 to 453 in the sample at 04:19:30Z, then stayed flat until isolated +1 increments around 04:24-04:25Z.

frontend-proxy's access log contains twelve 5xx responses between 04:15:31.789Z and 04:28:55.984Z, including six HTTP 500 "via_upstream" responses (21-byte body) between 04:17:43.286Z and 04:17:43.885Z on GET /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N (twice), /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4, /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM and POST /api/checkout, plus "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" on GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP at 04:17:39.360Z and GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4 at 04:18:33.332Z.

The frontend (otel-demo) recorded its own ERROR spans at the 04:19:30Z sample: 6 on CLIENT span grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, 5 on SERVER span GET /api/products/{productId}, 5 on internal span executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId], 1 on POST /api/checkout and 1 on its internal route, 1 on SERVER span POST, 5 on SERVER span GET, and 1 on internal span tcp.connect; all of these counters were flat before and after that sample.

Deployment product-catalog (otel-demo) was rolled out at 04:17:39-43Z: the Deployment scaled ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1 and it created pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 at 04:17:39Z (container started 04:17:42Z), then pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp reported "Stopping container product-catalog" at 04:17:43Z, ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc deleted it at 04:17:43Z and the Deployment scaled that ReplicaSet from 1 to 0.

The two product-catalog ReplicaSets have byte-identical pod templates (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, same env including PRODUCT_CATALOG_RELOAD_INTERVAL=10 and GEMLIMIT-style GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB, same ConfigMap volume product-catalog-products) except that the new ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 carries pod annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:17:39Z; the replacement pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 is Ready (lastTransitionTime 04:17:43Z) with restartCount 0 and imageID ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:5af68959300c804e71176aa8071abd30d1209771762e006c9fe7843561ab7b6a.

product-catalog's own span telemetry shows no error status: all of its span-metric series carry status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (17,925 span increase over the 30 minutes ending 04:40Z) and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series exists for the service; its logs in 04:17-04:45Z read as repeated "Product Found" lines interleaved with "Reloading Product Catalog..." and "Loaded 10 products".

The frontend's GetProduct client ERROR counter stayed at 6 from 04:20Z through 04:40Z with no further increment, while frontend-proxy's ingress ERROR counter continued to creep from 526 to 532 over the same period; the proxy also logged 503 UC responses at 04:23:36.724Z (GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO), 04:24:07.489Z (GET /api/recommendations?productIds=0PUK6V6EV0) and 04:28:55.984Z (GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N).

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo (created 2026-11-17T03:44:37Z) holds demo.flagd.json in which productCatalogFailure has defaultVariant "on" (description "Fail product catalog service on a specific product", variants off=false/on=true, state ENABLED) while every other flag defaults to "off"; ConfigMap product-catalog-products was also created 03:44:37Z and contains a single products.json key of 7,316 bytes.

All 21 otel-demo pods report phase Running and Ready with restartCount 0; only the product-catalog pod is younger than the incident (startTime 2026-11-17T04:17:39Z), the rest started at 03:44Z (flagd at 03:46:26Z), and the frontend Deployment is still at deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1 with image demo:2.1.3-frontend and limits cpu 100m/memory 200Mi.

In the 04:10-04:35Z window only seven services returned STATUS_CODE_ERROR series: frontend-proxy and frontend (with the burst at the 04:19:30Z sample), plus isolated 2-error samples on ad (around 04:12:30Z and 04:22:30Z), fraud-detection (around 04:21Z), recommendation (around 04:27Z), and zero-valued series for accounting and payment; no ERROR series appeared for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote or shipping.

The failed requests were caused by the product-catalog pod replacement: the frontend's live gRPC channel to the old product-catalog pod was broken when that pod was stopped at 04:17:43Z, so its GetProduct calls failed (6 ERROR client spans, one tcp.connect ERROR), the frontend answered those product-page and checkout requests with HTTP 500 (6 x 500 in 600 ms at 04:17:43Z) and terminated other product-route connections (503 UC), which is what frontend-proxy's error counters registered.

The alert's reported value 0.01111111111111111 corresponds to 7 failing requests out of about 630 in its evaluation window (7/630 = 0.011111...), matching the 7 errors registered in frontend-proxy's ingress error counter at the 04:19:30Z sample (6 HTTP 500 plus the 503 at 04:18:33Z); an alerting rule with a 5-minute 'for' would then start firing at 04:25:04Z, one evaluation after the 04:20:04Z deviation. The rule expression itself is not verifiable in this Prometheus.

The 503 UC "upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" responses on product and recommendation routes that appear before the rollout (04:15:31.789Z, 04:17:39.360Z) and continue after it (04:23:36.724Z, 04:24:07.489Z, 04:28:55.984Z) are a separate, ongoing failure mode of the frontend rather than an effect of the product-catalog restart; its cause is not established by the available evidence.

The flagd setting productCatalogFailure="on" is not supported as the cause of this burst: the failing requests cover at least five distinct product IDs (HQTGWGPNH4, 66VCHSJNUP, LS4PSXUNUM, 2ZYFJ3GM2N, L9ECAV7KIM), the frontend's GetProduct ERROR counter stopped at 6 and did not increase for the following 20 minutes, and product-catalog recorded no ERROR span status in its span metrics and its logs in the window read as repeated "Product Found" / "Reloading Product Catalog..." / "Loaded 10 products".

No other otel-demo service showed error evidence tied to this burst: cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in 04:10-04:35Z, and the isolated 2-error samples on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation fall at times that do not coincide with the 04:19:30Z frontend/frontend-proxy burst.

The apparent collapse of product-catalog span volume to 122 spans/min at the 04:19:30Z sample is rejected as a measurement artifact, not a traffic stop: the raw counters show the old per-pod instance 2fc46094-8ea7-40c9-8613-6366367ced0d at 20673 and the new instance d823523f-82fb-4691-b07c-79402ae7d795 (which equals pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9's uid) beginning at 672 in the same sample, i.e., a service-instance-id transition that increase() undercounts.
Determine who or what issued the rollout restart of Deployment product-catalog at 04:17:39Z (the change-history integration is not available in this Run; cluster audit logs would settle it).

Harden the single-replica rollout path so a product-catalog pod change cannot surface as 5xx: add a PodDisruptionBudget and graceful drain (preStop/terminationGracePeriod), keep the old endpoint until the new pod is Ready, and give the frontend's gRPC client retry/backoff so transient UNAVAILABLE on GetProduct does not become HTTP 500.

Review the fault-injection flag file in ConfigMap flagd-config: productCatalogFailure is defaultVariant "on" while every other flag is "off"; it did not explain this burst but it is an armed fault injector and should normally be "off" outside test scenarios.

Verify the RequestErrorRate rule (expression, threshold, evaluation window and 'for') in the Prometheus/Alertmanager that owns it, since the rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus and the exact 0.0111 derivation could not be reproduced; also investigate the recurring 503 UC connection terminations on /api/products/* and /api/recommendations that predate and outlast the rollout.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: the list_prometheus_rules query with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the rule's expression, threshold, evaluation window and 'for' duration are unverified and the reported 0.01111111111111111 could not be reproduced exactly.

The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what triggered the kubectl rollout restart of Deployment product-catalog at 04:17:39Z (pod annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) is unknown.

A regex-filtered read of all 11,235 product-catalog log lines in 04:17-04:45Z for error|fail|invalid|exception|not found|refused returned nothing (query status no_data with 11,235 lines read); that absence only shows no such line matched, and no product-catalog error line was observed.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw produced no readable log lines: two reads in 04:00-04:45Z and 04:19:00-04:20:30Z returned nothing (query status no_data, 0 bytes read), so the frontend's own error messages for the six 500s are unknown.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy at 04:25:00-04:25:02Z or 04:18:20-04:18:40Z (both queries status no_data), so no trace-level parent/child evidence exists for the failing requests; the child-span attribution rests on spanmetrics and access logs.

Searches for traces tagged error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR" or http.status_code="503" on frontend and frontend-proxy returned nothing (status no_data), so the spans' actual error/tag details for the failing requests are unknown.

The queries get_metric_names with match {__name__=~"http_.*"} and the instant query sum by (rpc_service,rpc_method,rpc_grpc_status_code) (increase(rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{...})) both returned no data, so HTTP-level and gRPC-status-level metrics for frontend-proxy/frontend are not available and error composition beyond spanmetrics is unknown.
The get_series query for kube_pod_container_info returned no data, so per-pod container image identity for otel-demo pods could not be compared beyond the pod status and ReplicaSet specs.

The cause of the recurring 503 UC 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses on /api/products/* and /api/recommendations (04:15:31Z, 04:23:36Z, 04:24:07Z, 04:28:55Z) is not identified; the available logs do not show which upstream connection was terminated or why.

Whether the alert is still firing after 04:25:04Z cannot be confirmed from the loaded rules or Alertmanager state; only the error metric series (frontend-proxy ingress ERROR rising from 526 to 532 up to 04:40Z) are available.

The spanmetrics series switched per-pod instance id (2fc46094-8ea7-40c9-8613-6366367ced0d to d823523f-82fb-4691-b07c-79402ae7d795) at the 04:19:30Z sample with an apparent export lag, so exact per-pod attribution of spans in the 04:17-04:20Z window is uncertain.
Secrets were not readable, but no conclusion here depends on secret values.
next_steps: Ask the platform/change process to confirm the operator or automation behind the rollout restart of Deployment product-catalog at 2026-11-17T04:17:39Z (audit log / change history).
Fetch the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its alert history from the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that fired it to confirm the evaluation window and 'for' duration.
Instrument or log the frontend's gRPC client errors (target endpoint, status code) so connection-level failures to product-catalog are directly attributable in future incidents.
Add rollout protection for single-replica dependencies (PodDisruptionBudget, preStop/graceful drain, wait-for-ready endpoints) and client retries for UNAVAILABLE.
Open a separate investigation for the recurring 503 UC connection terminations on product and recommendation routes, including frontend resource limits and keep-alive settings.
